subject: Error in prepping summary statistics for multivariate GWAS

messages.author: a496ef30cb6c9532
messages.subject: Error in prepping summary statistics for multivariate GWAS
parts:
Hello,

When I prep the summary statistics for multivariate GWAS (code below): 
prop<-c(NA,NA,NA,NA)
se.logit <-c(F, F, F, F)
Hail<-c(F, F, F, F)
files <- list("OUD_GWAS_SEM.txt", "PAU_GWAS_SEM.txt", "Tob_GWAS_SEM.txt", "CUD_GWAS_SEM.txt")
ref <- "reference.1000G.maf.0.005.txt.gz"

Addiction <- sumstats(files=files,ref=ref,trait.names=c("OUD", "PAU", "Tob", "CUD"),se.logit=se.logit, OLS = NULL,linprob=Hail,prop=prop,keep.indel=FALSE,parallel=TRUE,cores=16)


I get the error: 

Error: `x` and `y` must share the same src, set `copy` = TRUE (may be slow).

Run `rlang::last_error()` to see where the error occurred.

In addition: Warning message:

In mclapply(X = 1:length, FUN = function(X) { :

  scheduled cores 4, 2 encountered errors in user code, all values of the jobs will be affected



I didn't see this anywhere else on the forum, so I thought I would post here.  The files all have the same columns (though not always in the same order) and they are:

SNP A1 A2 Effect SE N P

Best,

Alex

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: Error in prepping summary statistics for multivariate GWAS
parts:
Hi Alex, 

I think the issue here is the white spacing in the sub argument you specified was causing the function to not match any of the lavaan representations of that parameter which remove all white spacing. That is ultimately the fault of the function, which should be catching something like that. With that said, I've updated the userGWAS function to automatically remove the white spacing which should produce a data.frame with entries when run in parallel and should not produce that error message when run in serial. Of course, if you are still having issues let us know but try redownloading the package, restarting R, and giving it a go. 

Thanks!
 -Andrew
